title: Polar Chess Expedition brings the first FIDE-rated chess tournament to Antarctica and the South Pole
summary: Six chess players representing all six inhabited continents will travel to Antarctica and the Geographic South Pole this Antarctic summer season to attempt the Polar Chess Expedition, the most geographically extreme chess tournament ever played. The FIDE-rated tournament will be played at rapid chess time control, with every round broadcast live. The play opens with early rounds on the Antarctic ice before culminating at 90° South, in an attempt to be certified as the southernmost chess tournament ever played. The six players each represent a different continent, and every player also serves their national or regional chess federation in some capacity: Aung Kyaw Moe, Candidate Master (Myanmar), Asia Damaris Abarca González, Woman FIDE Master (Chile), South America Jesse February, Woman International Master (South Africa), Africa Nigel Short, FIDE Grandmaster (England), Europe Shaun Press, FIDE Master (Papua New Guinea), Oceania Tris-Ann Richards, Woman Candidate Master (Saint Lucia), North America The field is led by Grandmaster Nigel Short of England, who in 1993 became the first Englishman in over a century to challenge for the World Chess Championship, taking on Garry Kasparov. Nigel currently serves as FIDE’s Director for Chess Development and lends the event both competitive weight and international recognition. The story behind the Polar Chess Expedition The idea took root two years ago when Aung came across an interview in which Nigel mentioned that he had won tournaments on every continent except Antarctica. “I’ve won tournaments on six continents. Antarctica is the one still missing,” said Nigel. Aung decided to embark on the project. Together with Nigel, they spoke to national chess federations across all six continents, turning a shared idea into a FIDE-rated tournament. “Nigel had the idea; my job was to make it real. Now it is, and we’re taking it to the end of the earth,” says Aung. Two of the players sum up the appeal of the challenge in their own words. “I live by a simple rule: If something scares you a little, it’s probably worth doing. By that measure, chess at the bottom of the world was never really a question,” said Jesse February, the tournament’s Africa representative. “Chess has taken me to some strange places over the years. This might be the first one where the biggest opponent isn’t across the board; it’s the weather,” said Shaun Press, representing Oceania. World record attempt: southernmost chess tournament ever played The Polar Chess Expedition is aiming to set a new world record. Potential record categories include the southernmost chess tournament ever played and the first chess event to bring players representing all six inhabited continents to the Geographic South Pole. For two of the players carrying continents to a chessboard for the first time, the record is personal as much as historic. “Saint Lucia is a small island, but chess has never asked me to think small. Representing my country, and an entire continent, is proof you can do big things from small places; there’s no ceiling on where the game can take you,” said Tris-Ann Richards, representing North America. “Chess has always been a bigger board than the one in front of you. Carrying South America to the bottom of the earth is just the latest way I’ve found to keep playing for something larger than myself,” says Damaris Abarca González, representing South America. About the Polar Chess Expedition The Polar Chess Expedition is a FIDE-rated chess tournament staged across Antarctica and the Geographic South Pole in an attempt to set a new world record as the most geographically extreme chess tournament in history. The six players are Nigel Short (England), Aung Kyaw Moe (Myanmar), Jesse February (South Africa), Shaun Press (Papua New Guinea), TrisAnn Richards (Saint Lucia), and Damaris Abarca González (Chile), each representing a different continent. For more information, contact Sylvia Mckaige(sylvia.mckaige@salweengroup.com) Official website: https://polarchessexpedition.com/

title: GCL 2026, Day 3: Alpine APL Pipers seize the lead
summary: The Monday matches completely reshaped the standings in the fourth edition of the Global Chess League. Despite losing their first match of the day, Alpine APL Pipers climbed to the top spot after crushing the former leaders, FYERS American Gambits. Triveni Continental Kings put themselves on the scoreboard, posting their first team victory over PBG Alaskan Knights. After Day 3, as many as four teams are sitting on 6 matchpoints each, with the Gambits holding second place thanks to a greater number of gamepoints. Let’s take a closer look at today’s action. Magnus Carlsen ground down his predecessor on the chess throne, Viswanathan Anand, on the Icon board, but it did not help the Pipers seal the match. The Knights roared back on Superstar boards with Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus, and Nino Batsiashvili pulling off crucial victories over Vidit Gujrathi and Humpy Koneru, respectively, to tip the balance in their favor. Many expected a close match here, but somewhat surprisingly that was not the case. The Mumba Masters dominated the proceedings: Pranesh M, Carissa Yip and Bardiya Daneshvar all won their games with White, securing a landslide victory for their team. The Ganges did not manage a single win and have suffered their heaviest setback in the event so far. FYERS American Gambits, who seemed unstoppable after Day 1, were handed their second consecutive defeat, which relegated them to second place in the standings. Vidit Gujrathi, Humpy Koneru and Volodar Murzin got the job done for the Pipers, all scoring victories with the black pieces. Notably, playing with White on all boards, the Gambits failed to win a single game. The Kings desperately needed a win to join the race for the title, and the team rose to the occasion, recording their first victory in the event. Wei Yi punished Arjun Erigaisi for snatching a “poisoned” pawn, scoring his first victory in four games. Aravindh Chithambaram followed Wei’s lead, outplaying Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus in the Maroczy setup and delivering checkmate on move 52. After teams traded blows on the women’s board with Kateryna Lagno and Alexandra Kosteniuk emerging victorious and the game on the Icon and Prodigy boards ended in draws, the Kings broke their winless streak and scored three well-deserved matchpoints. Standings after Day 3 Schedule for Tuesday, September 8: Match 13: Ganges Grandmasters vs. PBG Alaskan KnightsMatch 14: FYERS American Gambits vs. CheQ Mumba MastersMatch 15: Triveni Continental Kings vs. Alpine APL PipersMatch 16: FYERS American Gambits vs. PBG Alaskan Knights About the Global Chess League The Global Chess League (GCL), a joint initiative between Tech Mahindra and FIDE, is the world’s first and largest official franchise league of its kind. The league brings together leading chess players from across the globe in a unique joint team format, with six players representing each franchise across Icons, Superstar Men, Superstar Women and Prodigies. Men and women compete together on the same team, with every board carrying equal value towards the team’s result. GCL has previously staged seasons in Dubai, London, and Mumbai and returns to India for Season 4 in Bengaluru. GCL official website: https://globalchessleague.com/
